result.summary:
This run is the third successor. It found the predecessor's worktree and branch, both clean and pushed. All 11 city sets (hanse, german, german_old) are real-time models built with the new "city" builder in tools/blender/ce3d/cities3d.py. They replace the Arcade-picture stand-ins at every city arrival from Kiel to Nürnberg. buildings3d.py was not touched, so AS4's models stay byte-identical.

This run did round 5 (looked at all real exports by day, at dusk and at night) and round 6. In round 6 the 60 m level pictures showed that round-top doors in lod0 were cut as rectangles, and the 2.8 m guild-house gateway was a ribbed garage gate. The fix in cities3d.py (commit 4b?) changes only those doors. Fachwerkzeile, Turmhaus, Barock and Giebelzeile were re-exported. Crane, office tower, Kontor and Speicher were re-exported as a check and came out byte-identical, which is the determinism proof.

Measured: outline IoU 0.987–0.999 (crane 0.922); 427–9,865 triangles in lod0, 2 draw calls per level; archive share 0.79 MB meshes and 5.25 MB textures.

Gates: validator OK, sprite geometry 86/86 identical, check-keys OK, Arcade 20/20 and 17/17 identical. Modern goldens S4 and S5 change because the new models appear; I looked at both and rewrote the list. A/B at Hamburg, Hannover and Würzburg: 9 runs, 0 script errors. The 10-second clip is recorded. run_tests: 749 tests; one music timing test fails (headless Arcade run that loads none of the new models).

Weakest points: shimmer and the level swap of the half-timbered houses, and railings that thin out from about 100 m.

result.quality_verdict: Good: at all three city arrivals Modern now shows the actual houses in place of flat Arcade pictures, in the same position and outline (IoU ≥0.987). Close up they have clearly more depth than the sprite: window reveals, timber framing as real members, jettied storeys, cornices, oriels, balconies with cut-out railings, arched doors, and shop windows with goods behind the glass. At night the same windows are lit as in Arcade, and the backs are closed. In the A/B pictures Modern looks clearly better, not just different, above all in Würzburg and Hamburg. Not yet good: in motion the houses shimmer 2–10× as much as the sprites (half-timbered row 1.3 % against 0.1 %). The level swap at 60 m changes 10–32 % of the pixels, so it is likely visible on the half-timbered houses. Railings thin out from about 100 m. At dusk fewer windows are lit than in Arcade (renderer). The tinted suburban houses stay white until R7 adds tinting for models. Small flaws: office-tower lobby at night, painted oriel windows. Missing: measurements on a real GPU and on the Steam Deck; the second half of the styles.

result.overall: Yes, the city buildings look visibly finer than the Arcade pictures. Nine of the eleven models are clearly finer and two (office tower, crane) are equal. At 10–100 m they have real depth: window reveals, timber framing as real beams, jettied upper storeys, cornices, window pediments, balconies with cut-out railings and shadows, and shop windows with goods behind the glass. In the race at Hamburg, Nürnberg and Hannover (picture comparisons I ran myself) they are sharper and more three-dimensional than Arcade. Their outlines match the Arcade pictures (overlap 0.987–0.999, measured), and the budgets are kept (at most 9,865 triangles, 0.79 MB meshes and 5.25 MB textures in the archive, measured). At 22:00 the same windows are lit as in Arcade, warm and irregular. They are not yet good enough for hours of city driving. In the old towns and the Hamburg centre, what passes at eye level is the side wall facing the road, and that wall has no openings: blank ground floors on the half-timbered and Baroque houses, and a 16 × 17 m blank wall on the Hanseatic gable row. Arcade shows facades with doors and windows at the same moment. On top of that, the half-timber beams shimmer 3–14× as much as the Arcade picture, the 60 m detail switch changes up to 32 % of the pixels, and railings vanish from about 75 m. In the race, two problems that are not in the models hurt the cities most. In bends the renderer's sight-corridor rule removes whole houses: in München one side of the street is empty. And until R7 adds tinting for models, Hamburg's suburbs show white houses instead of pink. My recommendation: the eleven models can go into the next test build, because they replace worse pictures and nothing is broken. The lead should decide the corridor question first, and a rework should add the side-wall openings first. Everything about a real GPU, the Steam Deck or how it feels to a player is inferred; I measured on llvmpipe only.

pipeline_issues: Highest-impact in-race problem, not caused by the models: in bends the props builder's drop_reason removes city houses and Arcade stand-ins. In München km 161.7–162.6 the whole left side of the street is empty; in Nürnberg km 103.6 the corner-turret house is missing. FIX-M2 B-01 left this open for the lead to decide, so the RINT-M2 merge will not fix it. Proposed: in city sections (limit ≤ 50) take the corridor chord from F2 at the allowed speed, or exempt buildings of a city rule.

Contract conflict: the bar says 'the generators ARE the look, never a new design' and also 'real depth where the camera sees it from the street'. The generators have no openings on exactly the side walls the 3D camera passes at eye level. Fixing K2 needs lead approval for close3d side-wall openings (sprite unchanged). AS5a2/AS5b sets (canal houses, terraces, Haussmann blocks) face the same question.
baked_cutout mips are generated at import with a box filter, so railing coverage cannot be kept. The coverage-preserving mip step needs an owner for bake.py or the import scripts.
A-16 asks for a dither cross-fade only for trees; city buildings change 15–32 % of their pixels at 60 m. R7 should cover buildings too.

Review tool caveat: the stand-in of prop_scene --look=race shows no window light at dusk or night, and at noon it is 11–23 % darker than lod1. Light and brightness can only be judged against Arcade in the race (ab_shot), not against the stand-in.

Machine time: one Modern ab_shot with two pictures took 11–21 min on the shared VM, and the drive clip took 3.7 s per frame. So Kassel and Würzburg at noon, Medium at noon and an in-race clip were not run; a 50 km/h test-street clip (k5_scene --mode=drive) stands in for the clip.
No departures could be checked: the race places props/city_* only at stage arrivals (my count, logs/census_k5.log).

result.summary:
This run started fresh from 63544b6; I found no earlier run to pick up. I first reproduced each review finding. Then I reworked the builder and exported all 11 city models again.

Fixed:
- K2 (high): the road-facing side walls are no longer blank. The half-timbered row, the guild house (now the whole side wall and gable), the Baroque house and the Hanseatic gable row have windows and doors in the style of their fronts. They are added through generator hooks, so the sprites stay the same (86 of 86 identical).
- K4: the oriel has real windows with casing, glazing bars and sill. Its corbel is now sandstone instead of a white cone.
- K7: railings no longer vanish in the small mip levels. The gaps carry alpha 0.4 and the colour of the wall behind, so at a distance the railing reads as a band. Brightness deviation per mip was up to 18 luma steps; it is now at most 2.3 (measured).
- K5 (partly): a frame ring painted inside each window's glass lowers the night brightness jump at the 60 m level switch (half-timbered row +9.0 → +5.0 %).
- K10: the house's far level has 1,406 instead of 2,526 triangles.

Not fixed: shimmer of the timber beams. It is unchanged at 1.2–1.4 % against 0.1 % for the sprite; narrower beams did not help. The level switch still changes 13–27 % of the pixels. Both need the renderer.

Gates: validator OK, sprite geometry 86/86, check-keys OK, determinism byte-identical. AS4's models, the bridge parts and the houseboat are byte-identical. Archive share is 0.82 MB meshes and 5.36 MB textures. Ten race A/B runs gave 0 script errors. Arcade is 20/20 and 17/17 identical. The Modern goldens S4 and S5 changed; I looked at both and wrote the list again. The test suite had one load-sensitive audio test fail; it passed when I re-ran it on its own.

result.quality_verdict:
Good: in the old towns and in Hamburg's centre, no windowless wall passes the road any more. The half-timbered, Baroque and gable houses show windows and doors with frames, glazing bars and steps on the side facing the road, lit at night like the front. The race pictures at Nürnberg and Hamburg show this clearly against the review state, and Modern now looks clearly better than Arcade there (looked at). The oriel reads as a real oriel. Railings stay visible as a band at 80–110 m instead of breaking into dots. The night jump at the level switch is smaller.

Not good yet: the timber beams still shimmer in motion, 10 times as much as the sprite (measured on llvmpipe; MSAA on a real GPU would soften this, inferred). The 60 m level switch still changes 13–27 % of the pixels. The house's lighter far level changes more pixels at the switch than before, although the hedges look the same by eye. The corbel is a smooth stone cone. The office lobby is flat at night.

The renderer issues hurt the city most: houses are missing in bends (München) and the suburbs are untinted. Missing: measurements on a real GPU and on the Steam Deck, and a race clip.

result.quality_verdict:
Gut (angesehen): Im Rennen ist Modern dort, wo Arcade eine flache Hausflanke vorbeischiebt, klar feiner. Das zeigen die Haussmann-Zeile mit durchgehenden Balkonen und Bogenläden mit Auslage, die Grachtenhaus-Flanken mit Schiebefenstern, das Maashaus-Erdgeschoss und die Berner Lauben als echte Arkaden. Front, Dach, Farben und Umriss entsprechen dem Sprite, die Häuser stehen an derselben Stelle. Tagsüber und in der Dämmerung wirkt das stimmig.

Noch nicht gut:
- Nachts sind die Schaufenster deutlich dunkler als in Arcade (gemessen). Das ist der schwächste Punkt; in Paris sieht der Spieler ihn sofort.
- Die Modelle flimmern 2–5-mal so stark wie die vorgefilterten Sprites (Geländer, Sprossen). Das ist sichtbar, aber nicht störend (gefolgert aus Messwerten, die Bewegung wurde nicht Bild für Bild angesehen).
- Bei 200–250 m sind die lod1-Fensterreihen heller als das Sprite.
- Die Bäume von Südhaus und Loire-Haus sind aus der Nähe Klumpen.
- Die Rückseiten von Eckhaus und Halsgiebelhaus sind blank (selten zu sehen).
- Es gibt keine Wandleuchten.

Alles zu echter GPU und Steam Deck ist gefolgert; gemessen wurde auf llvmpipe.

pipeline_issues: Vertrag ≤2 Aufrufe je Stufe zwingt 5 von 12 Modellen (907 Platzierungen) und 2 aus Charge 1 dazu, die ganze Fassade als baked_cutout (cull_disabled, discard, auch lod1) zu zeichnen, und verhindert AS3-Gartenbäume (leaves) im Modell – Leitung: 3 Oberflächen für Stadthäuser oder Anbau-Mechanismus in R7 (GPU-Kosten gefolgert).

Import-Mips (Box-Filter) der baked_cutout-Atlanten: Deckung wächst ab Mip 2 auf 1,2–4,2-fach (mit cut_fill), ohne cut_fill verschwand sie (Charge 1) – deckungserhaltende Mips in bake.py/Import brauchen eine Freigabe (offen seit KRITIK-5a1 K7).

Die Mip-Kette der gebackenen Atlanten macht ferne Fassaden 5–10 % heller und Fenster rosa-lila (p10 +13–23 Stufen, lod0 = lod1) – AS4Rs Schwäche wiederholt; Lösung vorgefilterte Fensterregion oder R7-Fernbild ab ~200 m.
Ladenlicht-Formel cities3d._display_mat ist mit Charge 1 geteilt: jede Korrektur erzwingt den Neu-Export aller 23 Stadthäuser – Leitung sollte K1–K4 in einer Nacharbeit bündeln.
Prüfszenen-Platzhalter hat eigenes Licht und nachts kein Fensterlicht: absolute Helligkeit und Nacht nur im Rennen vergleichbar; texel_k5 erfasst zurückgesetzte Wände erst mit K5_OUTER 4,5–8.

Die Basis von AS5a2 enthält FIX-M2 B-01 und den R6-Bauer city nicht: im A/B fehlen in Kurven Häuser (Lyon km 297,4, Bern km 302,7) und die Szenerie-Zäune/Mauern/Hecken (Brüssel, Vororte) – nach RINT-M2 dieselben Stellen wiederholen.
Eine neue Prüfhilfe k6_scene.gd --mode=lodcol (lod0/lod1/Sprite im selben Licht, mittlere Farbe und Fenster-p10) liegt in m1/KRITIK-5a2/kt/ – nützlich als Nachweis für die Fernfenster-Korrektur.
